newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs close sharply up on yen, interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs close sharply up on yen, interest rates.

text.p: Stocks rose to the highest close since October 28 on renewed hopes for benefits from a rising yen and falling local interest rates, brokers said.
The composite index gained 1.6 percent, or 12.24 points, to 775.01. It was the highest closing rate since October 28, when it stood at 780.08.
"Falling interest rates and the yen's fresh rebound today boosted buying, especially in securities and shipbuilding firms," said Koh Kyung-bae, analyst at Hyundai Securities.
South Korea's benchmark three-year corporate bond yields were trading at 11.38 percent on Monday, the lowest level in 12 months, bond market dealers said.
The Japanese yen rose to arond 111.80 per dollar on Monday in Tokyo, the lowest level since November, before quickly retreating to around 113 yen.
The sub-index for securities firms soared by 7.64 percent, or 104.85 points, to 1,476.52.
Brokers said investors believed the low interest rates would help boost earnings of securities firms which heavily depend on borrowings.
Almost all the securities firms rose to their daily limits. Daishin Securities rose 640 won to 8,690 and Daewoo Securities up 1,100 won to 15,000.
News on the yen's rise boosted buying in firms competing with Japanese makers in export markets. Daewoo Heavy Industries rose 330 won to 8,580 after hitting its new yearly high of 8,650.
